mappings.note: show they are zeroes is substitution (LO-1); verify the relationship is the coefficient check (LO-2). Both halves are stated in the question

sorts ten expressions into polynomials and non-polynomials and counts the quadratics. This is the definition and degree of a polynomial -- no learning outcome in this frame touches either, so only the goal-level code fits
splits the middle term of 5x^2 + 8x - 4 (LO-1) and then checks sum and product against the coefficients (LO-2)
factorises x(x - 2 root2) for the zeroes (LO-1) and verifies both relations, including the product being 0 (LO-2)
solves the sum/difference pair for the two zeroes, then builds x^2 - 24x + 128; the deliverable is the polynomial, so LO-3

uses all three cubic coefficient relations to evaluate the sum of reciprocals. LO-2 states only the quadratic pair, so the cubic symmetric functions are an extension of it -- the nearest outcome by a wide margin

recovers the divisor from dividend = divisor x quotient + remainder, finishing by factorising x^2 + 7x + 10. The division algorithm has no outcome in this frame; the factorised-form link in C-2.3-LO-1 is the only part of it any outcome names

x + 7 is a factor exactly when -7 is a zero -- the factor-root equivalence LO-1 of C-2.3 states, here on a quartic. Cited over C-2.1-LO-1 because the question is about divisibility, not about finding zeroes
g(x) recovered by dividing a quartic by a quadratic. Nothing factorises to roots and no zero appears, so even C-2.3-LO-1 does not reach it; the division algorithm is simply absent from this frame
(alpha-beta)^2 = (alpha+beta)^2 - 4 alpha beta with both substituted from coefficients; the long-form twin of the MCQ, same outcome
the divisor is factorised into (x+4)(x+3), its roots forced to be zeroes of f, and p and q solved for -- the factorised-form-to-roots link driving a divisibility condition
the given relation is rewritten as (alpha+beta)^2 - alpha beta and evaluated from the coefficients to find k
clears fractions, splits the middle term for the zeroes (LO-1), then verifies both coefficient relations (LO-2)
the transformed zeroes have their sum and product computed symbolically (LO-2) before the new polynomial is assembled (LO-3)
same two-stage shape on 1 + beta/alpha and 1 + alpha/beta; relations first, construction second
reciprocal zeroes fix a through the product relation, then the sum relation gives a quadratic in beta; entirely coefficient relations, no construction asked
five symmetric expressions in the zeroes, all evaluated from -b/a and c/a; the zeroes are complex and deliberately never found, which rules LO-1 out
the sum relation plus the given difference give both zeroes, then the product relation gives k; LO-2 throughout
same sum-and-difference method to recover k from the product; short twin of q723666
builds a cubic volume model from a verbal description, which no outcome covers (CG-2), then solves x^3 + x^2 - 6x = 18 by locating a root (C-2.3-LO-1)
expands (x+4)^3 as a model and evaluates it, once directly and once by the remainder theorem. Neither polynomial modelling nor the remainder theorem appears anywhere in this frame

the base dimensions come from factorising V(x) = x(x+3)(x+8), which is the factorised-form-to-roots outcome; the remainder-theorem evaluation and the capacity question have no outcome, hence CG-2 alongside
constructs V(x) for a folded pan and evaluates it by the remainder theorem; model building plus remainder theorem, neither of which any outcome names
builds V(x) and a cost function C(x) from a square sheet; nothing is factorised and no zero is sought, so no learning outcome applies
the side of the square bottom is read from V = b(b-3)^2, a factorised-form deduction (C-2.3-LO-1); the remainder-theorem evaluations in the later parts have no outcome
